findings.claim: The replacement promise is still incomplete and contains incompatible acceptance requirements. A revision is needed before an executor can implement one unambiguous contract.

manifestations.detail: Step 1 constructs, validates and encodes the backup before the protected call. Its failure outcome is undefined. The condition in 1a that the CLI actually returns also excludes an ordinary exception escaping this preparation, defeating the claimed outer boundary. The backup description must distinguish nullable collected timestamps from mandatory tao_luc and cong_cu metadata: context identity alone, or all timestamps null, does not satisfy the unchanged schema.

Acceptance 2 requires every listed positive case to contain LỖI BẤT NGỜ: <class>, including 2(e). But 2(e) also requires byte equality with the precomputed backup, whose required reason is LỖI BẤT NGỜ trong lệnh thu. Those conditions cannot both hold.

Step 1c.3 and 2(g) assert no file when all writes fail. Failed writes can leave a partial file or preserve an existing green file. The I/O carve-out in 1b and this absolute absence assertion disagree. Printing the final stderr line can itself fail; no resulting disposition is defined. The contract does not specify fresh versus pre-existing output or errors before versus after truncation.

evidence.observed: Executable model of the stated ordering: preparation KeyError escapes with no receipt; fallback-validation failure yields rc=1, valid receipt and exact backup bytes, but the class-specific reason assertion is false; failed partial writes leave 12 bytes; failure before opening preserves a pre-existing ok=true receipt; failing stderr raises BrokenPipeError. Context-only/all-timestamps-null variants fail the frozen schema. These are specification countermodels, not claims about an implemented wp1522 change.

Current production seams can independently raise RecursionError from X2, KeyError from X4 and MemoryError from X5. MemoryError is an Exception. Thus the main body is testable, but protecting it alone does not define preparation and last-resort outcomes.

suggested_fix.where: Revise SPEC contract 1a-1d and acceptance 2, because the conflicting policy is owned here; do not alter the frozen v1 schema to accommodate an incomplete backup.
suggested_fix.how: Define the covered execution interval and explicit preparation-failure disposition. Specify all mandatory backup metadata and exactly which timestamps are null. Give 2(e) its own generic-reason expectation. Specify observable output state for failed writes, including existing and partial output, and best-effort diagnostics; either require an appropriate atomic replacement/cleanup policy or explicitly retain these outcomes as excluded debt. Avoid using successful return as the condition that silently excuses uncaught bugs.
suggested_fix.locking_test_and_mutant: Exercise preparation, normal collector, enriched recovery, backup write and diagnostic failures separately, with fresh and existing output controls. A mutant leaving preparation outside the defined boundary must fail its named case; using the enriched reason in the fixed backup must fail byte equality; omitting replacement after a successful green write must fail 2(f); a partial-write mutant must fail the chosen final-file-state assertion. Check exact schema fields and distinguish interruption from ordinary exceptions.
suggested_fix.what_the_fix_may_spawn: Do not invent timestamps or tool hashes, broaden the carve-out to all programming errors, catch KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, change invalid-argument rc=2, leak exception text, or delete a pre-existing file without a defined policy. Preserve the historical class and its four prior occurrences.

findings.claim: The frozen fixture suite does not independently lock the new year floor or the exact integer type of REST job run_id. Both requirements can be removed while all 486 checks still pass.

manifestations.detail: The 0999 case claims 0999-11-21T19:17:00Z, but November 21 of year 999 is Thursday. The actual preceding Saturday is November 16. Removing the year floor still produces C9.khung because the supplied frame is wrong, so the case passes for the wrong reason within the same predicate.

The new C4 case changes only the numeric run ID. Removing type(j.get("run_id")) is int leaves all fixtures passing and accepts a matching floating-point run_id. Acceptance 4 specifies missing and unequal IDs but no equal-value wrong-type case.

evidence.observed: Independent calendar calculation gives 0999-11-16T19:17:00Z. With that correct frame, v2 returns [C9] while the no-year-floor mutant returns []; the frozen wrong-frame case does not distinguish them.
For run_id=float(run.id), original v2 returns [C4]; the type-check-erasure mutant returns [].

suggested_fix.where: Revise the frozen 0999 fixture and add typed REST-job fixtures in wp1522-r1/hop_dong/fixture.json; update the SPEC hashes/counts and explicit targeted mutation obligations before freezing. The executor is forbidden to repair these artifacts itself.
suggested_fix.how: Use an otherwise correct 0999 cron frame to isolate rejection solely by the year policy. Add matching-int positive, matching-float negative and missing-ID controls, then carry the same domain into collector acceptance. Test removal of the year guard and removal of only the integer guard separately from removal of the entire C9/C4 predicate.
suggested_fix.locking_test_and_mutant: Require the corrected 0999 case to kill return t in place of the year-floor return, and the equal-float case to kill removal of the exact-int conjunct. Record the exact target case and observed predicate. Retain the independently verified C3 isolation and the existing unequal-ID mutant.
suggested_fix.what_the_fix_may_spawn: Updating frozen cases changes hashes/counts and invalidates any #1521 measurement key. Keep v1 artifacts byte-identical for B2; avoid introducing a second C3 violation or allowing malformed dates through schema/calendar checks.
